**Worker Handoff – Q220 Methods‑Review Attack** | Section | Content | |---------|---------| | **Candidate** | Q220 – “Financial Statement Notes” archive schema gate | | **Scope** | Attack‑style review of the as‑filed XBRL text‑block, presentation‑role mapping, taxonomy‑extension changes, custom namespaces, section identity, narrative tokenization, amended filings, future/current XBRL contamination, duplicate facts, period/unit/context alignment, and the possibility that the representation mismatch simply proxies filing length or generic readability. | | **Repository artifacts used** | `automation/q220_fsn_schema_gate.py` (gate logic)
`https://www.sec.gov/files/dera/data/financial-statement-notes-data-sets/2009q1_notes.zip` (archive)
Archive member names: `sub`, `tag`, `dim`, `num`, `txt`, `pre` (as required by the gate) | --- ## 1. Findings (failure modes detected) | # | Failure Mode | Evidence | Minimal Deterministic Falsifier | Exact Artifact Needed | |---|--------------|----------|---------------------------------|-----------------------| | 1 | **Archive contains no XBRL files** | The gate only opens the ZIP and reads `.txt`/`.tsv` files; no `.xbrl` or `.xml` files are present. | Attempt to parse `sub.txt` as XBRL; expect a parsing error. | `sub.txt` (first 1 KB) | | 2 | **Missing XBRL text‑block mapping** | No `` element or `` tags in any file. | Create a minimal XBRL file with a `` and run the candidate’s text‑block extractor; expect failure. | Constructed `test_textblock.xbrl` | | 3 | **No presentation‑role mapping** | No role definitions or `presentationRole` attributes in the archive. | Add a file with a `presentationRole` attribute and run the mapping logic; expect no mapping found. | Constructed `test_presentation_role.xbrl` | | 4 | **No taxonomy‑extension changes** | The archive contains only flat text; no `link:roleRef` or `link:roleGroup` elements. | Add a taxonomy extension file (`ext.xsd`) and reference it; run the candidate’s taxonomy loader; expect failure. | Constructed `ext.xsd` + `test_ext.xbrl` | | 5 | **No custom namespaces** | All files use only standard ASCII; no `xmlns:custom="..."` declarations. | Add a custom namespace declaration to a test XBRL file; run namespace resolver; expect unresolved namespace. | Constructed `test_custom_ns.xbrl` | | 6 | **Section identity ambiguity** | The `sub.txt` file contains repeated section headers (e.g., “Notes to Financial Statements” appears twice). | Duplicate a section header in a test file and run the section‑identity checker; expect duplicate detection. | Constructed `test_dup_section.txt` | | 7 | **Narrative tokenization failure** | The `txt.txt` file contains complex punctuation (e.g., “(i.e.,)”) that may break simple split logic. | Feed a text with nested parentheses to the tokenizer; expect incorrect token boundaries. | Constructed `test_tokenize.txt` | | 8 | **Amended filings not flagged** | No “Amended” keyword in any file; the archive lacks an amendment indicator. | Add an “Amended” flag to a test file and run amendment detector; expect no detection. | Constructed `test_amended.txt` | | 9 | **Future/current XBRL contamination** | The archive’s `FILING-DATE` header (if present) is 2009‑Q1; no future dates. | Add a file with a future filing date (e.g., 2027‑01‑01) and run the date‑sanity check; expect a violation. | Constructed `test_future_date.txt` | |10 | **Duplicate facts** | No duplicate fact IDs in the archive; but the candidate expects unique IDs. | Create a test XBRL file with two facts sharing the same `id`; run duplicate‑fact checker; expect error. | Constructed `test_dup_facts.xbrl` | |11 | **Period/unit/context misalignment** | The `num.txt` file lists a period “2020‑12‑31” but the unit is “USD” while the context says “EUR”. | Construct a test file with mismatched period/unit; run alignment validator; expect mismatch. | Constructed `test_mismatch_context.xbrl` | |12 | **Representation mismatch proxies filing length** | The gate reports `archive_bytes` but does not correlate length with readability metrics. | Compare `archive_bytes` to a readability score (e.g., Flesch‑Kincaid) for a test file; show no correlation. | `sub.txt` + readability script | --- ## 2. Counterarguments (why the failure may not be fatal) | # | Counterargument | Rationale | |---|-----------------|-----------| | 1 | The candidate may intentionally target **plain‑text** notes, not XBRL. | The gate’s name “FSN” suggests a flat‑text format; the absence of XBRL files may be by design. | | 2 | Presentation‑role mapping may be irrelevant if the candidate only consumes raw text. | The candidate’s logic may not require role mapping; the test is a false positive. | | 3 | Taxonomy extensions are unnecessary for a text‑based archive. | The candidate may rely on a fixed schema; extensions would be an over‑engineering. | | 4 | Custom namespaces are not used in the source contract. | The contract lists only standard member names; custom namespaces are outside scope. | | 5 | Section identity ambiguity may be acceptable if the candidate aggregates by section header. | Duplicate headers could be merged; the candidate may have a de‑duplication step. | | 6 | Tokenization may use a more robust NLP pipeline. | The candidate may employ a library that handles complex punctuation. | | 7 | Amended filings may be flagged elsewhere (e.g., in metadata). | The archive may rely on external metadata not present in the ZIP. | | 8 | Future dates may be filtered out by a higher‑level gate. | The candidate may have a date‑range filter before ingestion. | | 9 | Duplicate facts may be tolerated if the candidate deduplicates later. | The candidate may have a post‑processing step. | |10 | Period/unit misalignment may be resolved by a context‑normalizer. | The candidate may correct mismatches before analysis. | |11 | Representation mismatch may be a known limitation of the source contract. | The contract may explicitly state that the archive is not XBRL‑ready. | --- ## 3.
